external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and can log in to the build runner to start a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be used to start a manual rebuild.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token when calling the deploy controller.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release record for the estate and responds to store server release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in the back office at each store that runs the till software as a container and updates it when a new release is available.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: The description refers to approximately 1,200 store servers.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: The source control server receiving developer branches and containing the merge to main that starts a build.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: A registry in the build environment receiving finished container images tagged with commit SHA values and serving image pulls from store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: public package registry
data_stores.description: The public internet registry reached during dependency resolution.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes branches to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source associated with a merge from the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: kick rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: The manual rebuild path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes a finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: Finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: The image SHA to make the current release

data_flows.name: check release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running release differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of store servers reached over the retail WAN.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The developer is assigned to the corporate network zone because the described developer interactions are with the corporate git server and build pipeline.
assumptions.basis: The source places the git server on the corporate network and describes developers interacting with the corporate build pipeline, but does not explicitly state the developers' network zone.
